entrada.texto:
Privacy-Preserving Vaccine Supply Chain 
Management Leveraging Blockchain and 
Self-Sovereign Identity
Brijesh Kumar Chaurasia1, Nikita Tiwari 2*, and Nikhil Pateria3* 
1 Department of Computer Science and Engineering,
Pranveer Singh Institute of Technology, Kanpur, UP, INDIA
2School of Computer Science, 
University of Petroleum and Energy Studies, Dehradun, UK INDIA
3Department of AI & ML,
Manipal University Jaipur, Jaipur, Rajasthan, INDIA
*Corresponding Author
*nikita.tiwari25@gmail.com
*nikhil.pateria@jaipur.manipal.edu
Abstract. Blockchain technology’s potential to enhance 
efficiency, security, and transparency has attracted a lot of 
attention to its integration into vaccination supply chain 
management in recent years. This work presents a 
comprehensive study on leveraging self-sovereign identity 
(SSI), blockchain, and privacy-preserving techniques to 
optimize vaccine distribution. We conduct a comparative 
analysis of existing blockchain-based frameworks, evaluating 
their effectiveness in addressing key challenges such as 
traceability, counterfeit prevention, and data privacy. The 
empirical results prove the efficacy of the proposed supply 
chain framework. Additionally, we identify and discuss critical 
challenges current systems face, including scalability issues, 
interoperability constraints, and privacy concerns. Our findings 
provide a robust foundation for future research and 
development in the field, proposing potential improvements and 
strategies to overcome the identified challenges.
Keywords: Blockchain, Supply Chain Management, Self-
Sovereign Identity (SSI), Traceability, Counterfeit Prevention, 
and Interoperability.

resposta.resumo: O artigo apresenta um estudo que combina blockchain, identidade auto-soberana (SSI) e técnicas de preservação de privacidade para melhorar a cadeia de suprimentos de vacinas. Os autores comparam frameworks baseados em blockchain, destacando benefícios em rastreabilidade, prevenção de falsificações e privacidade dos dados. Resultados empíricos indicam eficácia da solução proposta, embora reconheçam desafios de escalabilidade, interoperabilidade e privacidade que precisam ser superados.
